To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

both motivated and unmotivated processes influence the organizational identity categorizations that constituent groups find most salient, and that these processes operate through two distinct pathways.

constituent groups vary in their perceptions about the most salient organizational identity categorization due to both motivated and spontaneous cognitive processes, with the latter being more influential than the former.
both self-enhancement motives and spontaneous cognitions can explain variation in organizational identity categorization.

the question of why organizational identity categorizations vary across constituent groups.
explaining why organizational members often differ in their perceptions of what aspects of their organization’s identity are most salient.
how and why organizational identity categorizations vary among organizational constituents.

the organizational identity of an organization is the set of attributes that the organization wishes to be associated with and that the organization wants to be known for.

the organizational identity is a set of shared beliefs and perceptions held by members of an organization about the organization’s internal and external characteristics, its history, and the role it serves in the world.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the more we know about the organizational identity categorizations of different constituent groups, the better we can understand the organizational identity that emerges from the collective of these groups.
the organizational identity of a firm is not a static entity, but rather, a fluid construct that is subject to change and interpretation.
organizational members do not necessarily perceive the organization’s identity in a manner that is consistent with the organization’s official identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to motivated processes, spontaneous processes also influence the different organizational identities that constituent groups find to have the most salience.
the spontaneous and motivated processes that influence organizational identity perceptions can operate independently, but also can operate jointly.
, when explaining variation in organizational identity categorization, it is important to consider the role that both motivated and spontaneous cognitions play.
